questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Internationalized UI Design”?
options: Internationalized UI Design helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Internationalized UI Design means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Internationalized UI Design removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Internationalized UI Design should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Internationalized UI Design helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Internationalized UI Design is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Text expansion and layout flexibility” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Text expansion and layout flexibility” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Text expansion and layout flexibility” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Text expansion and layout flexibility” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Text expansion and layout flexibility” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Text expansion and layout flexibility” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Text expansion and layout flexibility” under Internationalized UI Design. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Internationalized UI Design”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
